criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: Every frame is rendered on a dark field. Machine QA has no fails. The three reliefs report real height ranges: s5 64.5, s6 31.6 and s7 114, each with 5 to 6 materials and cast fractions of 0.10 to 0.39. Frames 1, 2, 5 and 7 are strong. S1 is the tractor on the diamond-tread deck with converging yellow rails, under a green signal. S5's six machined week grooves run to a primer clamp, with three shims. S7 sets a white bead inlay against a 500-stud primer row on clay. The art is held down by four frames. S4 is a frontal array of identical bobtails floating in black. The two end units of the near rank are cut to slivers, so a reader counts 18 whole trucks at 432 px, and the lower 40 percent is empty black. S6 is a large flat dark rectangle with a mid-height seam. Its copper $9M tick sits in the 30 unit gap at design x 112.7, so it reads as the loss bar's left edge. S8 casts a blue-violet fill over the trailer slab and cab side and shows no ground. S3's right half is dead apart from one bollard, and the boom reads as a kerb. The same kit grille faces the camera on frames 1, 2, 3, 4 and 9. This lands on the 7 descriptor, but more than one frame leans on a default, so it scores under 7.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: The deck runs in one floodlit night world with the key from the upper right. The reliefs are raked the same way. Primer carries one meaning, what the letter says will happen, on s3's stop bar, s5's clamp, s7's studs, s9's stalls and s6's $9M tick. The yard appears twice, on s4 and s9, as a real device. The value track holds dark with no strobe. The middle cluster of three orthographic reliefs (5, 6, 7) sits slightly apart from the spatial frames. S8's violet fill sits outside the neutral grade. That makes it clearly one deck, with one frame slightly outside.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every numeral traces. The checks: numeral_report has 20 examined with 0 problems, label_report 44 checked with 0, quantifier 96 surfaces with 0 and aggregate_report 0. compute.py regex-extracts every figure from claim quotes, and the FIG values in s4, s5, s6, s7 and s9 match figures.json. The drawn counts are true in code: 20 tractors, 6 grooves, 3 shims, 500 studs, 1,000 stalls with a kerb at 200, and loss over revenue at 3.415 px per million. The sources are primary, the SEC exhibit and Aurora IR. Last round's hard fail on s7, counting routes, is gone. Several phrasings run looser than the source. S3's 'Next, straight through the gate' overstates c6's 'automated navigation through security checkpoints', and the docket title repeats 'straight'. S2's 'which scale' is a loose reading of 'adapt to different scale configurations'. On s7, 'Aurora's own route' in the singular, with only one Aurora line drawn, invites a reader to believe Dallas to Houston is Aurora's only Texas route. The claims file's own rejected list shows that was not established either way, so the set is not named. The web edition opens with an uncited inference, 'a call a driver used to make at the side of the interstate', which c8 does not support. Two statements in the round 2 brief do not match the pixels. S6's $9M mark is measured from the billet's left edge (X0 = 82), not from 'the datum's left end', and the datum runs the full width from x 0. S4 does not 'show all 20' whole. Neither statement is published copy.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: A reader learns what Aurora told investors and where it touches Texas: Dallas to Houston, Charger's Dallas to Laredo plan and AUMOVIO in New Braunfels on s7. The decider is a company. The record item says public access is 'contact_only', with no body, no deadline and nothing a Texan can act on. The letter names no Texas weigh station, so the weigh station hook on s1 and s2 is generic until s7. The stake stays general: driverless trucks at your scale house. The caption's closing question carries most of the local stake.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The s1 cover hook earns the swipe, and s2 pays with the three calls at once. The declared turn at s5, 'About six weeks behind its own plan', lands, and s6's money follows it. S9 closes on the 20 trucks against the 1,000 field, with the EDGAR pointer. S8 (the beacon) is the one frame that could move, to sit after s3, without loss. It interrupts the move from the Texas map to the expectations close.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: The copy is clean and on register. It follows house rules: no colons, dates as ordinals with no year, no banned words, and 'can't' never 'cannot'. The caption's close, 'Has a Texas scale house weighed a driverless Aurora truck yet?', sounds like a Texan. S7's 'Routes drawn straight between places.' and s6's 'Third quarter revenue and operating loss at one scale.' are flat method notes, and the deck reads more like an investor letter summary than a Texan who knows the roads.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: The topic is distinct, and topics.json has no Aurora entry since October 4th. The treatment repeats recent moves. No. 52 (October 16th) carried a white driverless vehicle through a night deck. The kit truck appeared on no. 41. The one-unit-per-thing yard or field returns from nos. 56, 64 and 62. S5's machined rule echoes no. 53's 'machined rule'. Several moves are familiar.

named_defects: s4: two of the 20 tractors are cut to slivers by the frame edges, so 18 read whole at 432 px against a '20+ built' headline. The round 2 brief's claim that the frontal view 'shows all 20' does not match the render.

s6: the $9M copper tick is placed at X0 + L9, measured from the billet's left edge, while the brief said 'from the datum's left end'. At feed size the tick sits in the gap and reads as the loss bar's left edge.
s6: dead code leaves the in-bar groove path inert, and a mid-height seam splits the loss bar into what reads as two slabs.
s3: 'Next, straight through the gate' overstates c6, which says 'automated navigation through security checkpoints'.
s2: 'which scale' is looser than c9's 'adapt to different scale configurations'.
s7: 'Aurora's own route' in the singular, with only one Aurora line drawn, implies exclusivity that no claim establishes.
web edition intro: 'a call a driver used to make at the side of the interstate' is an uncited inference beyond c8.
storyboard says the station and gate are 'labelled as illustrations', but no slide carries such a label.
s8: blue-violet fill on the trailer slab and cab side is off the deck's neutral grade, and no ground is visible.
s9: the far kerb stops in empty dark, and the 800-stall span reads as a near-black band (bound audition frame, unchanged).
one_sentence_fix: Make the two measured frames show what they claim: recompose s4 so all twenty tractors stand whole inside a pool that fills the empty lower half, and give s6's $9 million a visible primer bracket from the billet's left edge.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: A frontal grid of identical bobtails floats in black. The near rank's two end units are cropped to slivers (18 whole at 432 px), and the lower 40 percent of the frame is empty dark.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Pull the camera back from z 56 to about z 64 and lower the look target so both end tractors of the near rank sit whole inside the frame. Let the ranks drop about 120 px so their pool, casts and stall stripes fill the empty lower third.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The loss bar is a flat dark rectangle with a seam that splits it in two. The copper $9M tick sits in the 30 unit gap and reads as the loss bar's start, not as a length, and the lower third is empty.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Cut a primer bracket into the datum running from the billet's left edge (X0) to X0 + L9 with end ticks, so the $9 million reads as a length three times the billet's, and delete the mid-height seam on the loss bar.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: A blue-violet fill on the trailer slab and cab side breaks the neutral grade. The primitive trailer front fills the left third, there is no ground, and the beacon is dim.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Move the camera forward and right so the trailer leaves frame and the cab corner and beacon own it. Set the fill to the deck's neutral flood, and bring the shoulder under the front wheel into the pool.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The right half is dead apart from one bollard. The boom reads as a kerb with no pivot or cabinet.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Add the boom's pivot housing and gate cabinet as a slide-local mesh at the boom's right end in the right third, lit by the headlamps.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The far kerb is a thin band that stops abruptly in empty dark, and the 800 stalls between the kerbs read as a near-black band.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Raise the camera on the mast and turn the look toward the yard's centre column so the whole far kerb sits inside the frame (requires a fresh audition review).
